title: Past perfect
note: had + past participle for the EARLIER of two past events. Czech has one past tense, so the Czech never picks the form - every gap carries a (lemma) cue per B11, James dropdown 2026-09-02. Scope: core sequencing + already/just/never/by the time + the over-correction guard (2 items whose answer is past simple, because Czech learners under-use this form and then over-use it) + a backshift card and one item, since the same form is what reported speech lands on (C47 shape: direct sentence, reported sentence, tense named beside each). 'd taught with the would warning - I'd + participle is had, I'd + plain verb is would (b1_used_to). Check is quiz only: a sort into earlier/later is solvable by reading 'had' off the chip, which is the B15 toll. Use is error-correction (E7); the over-correction items carry the *had made / *had walked errors. Past participle is pretaught at a2_present_perfect. First draft 2026-09-02, core half - thicken after smoke.

examples.en: When I arrived, the film **had** already started.
examples.cz: Když jsem přišel, film už začal.

examples.en: I couldn't get in because I **had** lost my key.
examples.cz: Nemohl jsem se dostat dovnitř, protože jsem ztratil klíč.

points: Both things are over. **had** marks which one happened first.

cards.title: Czech has one past tense
cards.title_cz: Čeština má jen jeden minulý čas
points: Czech uses the same past form for both events, so nothing in the Czech tells you which came first. English marks it with **had**.

rows: When I arrived, the film **had** started.
The train **had** left before we got there.
I didn't recognise her — she **had** cut her hair.

cards.title: already · just · never · by the time
cards.title_cz: already · just · never · by the time

rows: We **had already** eaten when they arrived.
He **had just** finished when I called.
**By** the time we got there, the train had left.

points: These words sit between **had** and the participle.

cards.title: When you don't need it

rows: already in order — past simple twice
She opened the door **and** walked in.
already in order — past simple twice
When I got up, my wife **had** made coffee.
out of order — the coffee came first

points: If the events are told **in order**, past simple is enough.
Use **had** when you go back to something earlier.

rows: a wish or a request — a different word

cards.title: Reporting what someone said

rows: He said he **had** seen her. *past perfect*

points: Reporting moves the verb one step back in time, and past perfect is where it lands.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: Two traps: leaving **had** out, and putting it in when the events are already in order.

rows: ~~When I arrived, the film already started.~~
When I arrived, the film **had** already started.
~~I couldn't get in because I lost my key.~~
I couldn't get in because I **had** lost my key.
~~I got up and had made coffee.~~

items.en: When I arrived, the film had already started.
items.cz: Když jsem přišel, film už začal.
items.gap: When I arrived, the film ____. (already / start)
accepts: When I arrived, the film had already started.
items.wrong: When I arrived, the film already started.
items.explanation: The film started **before** I arrived, so the film takes **had** + started.
items.explanation_cz: Film začal **dřív**, než jsem přišel, takže má **had** + started.

items.en: She had never seen the sea before that day.
items.cz: Do toho dne nikdy neviděla moře.
items.gap: She ____ the sea before that day. (never / see)
accepts: She had never seen the sea before that day.
items.wrong: She had never saw the sea before that day.
items.explanation: **never** sits between had and the participle: had **never** seen. The participle of see is **seen**.
items.explanation_cz: **never** stojí mezi had a příčestím: had **never** seen. Příčestí od see je **seen**.

items.en: I couldn't get in because I had lost my key.
items.cz: Nemohl jsem se dostat dovnitř, protože jsem ztratil klíč.
items.gap: I couldn't get in because I ____ my key. (lose)
accepts: I couldn't get in because I had lost my key.
I could not get in because I had lost my key.
items.wrong: I couldn't get in because I lost my key.
items.explanation: Losing the key happened **before** the locked door, so it takes **had** lost.
items.explanation_cz: Ztráta klíče se stala **dřív** než zamčené dveře, proto **had** lost.

items.en: By the time we got to the station, the train had left.
items.cz: Než jsme došli na nádraží, vlak odjel.
items.gap: By the time we got to the station, the train ____. (leave)
accepts: By the time we got to the station, the train had left.
items.wrong: By the time we got to the station, the train left.
items.explanation: **By the time** always looks back at something finished earlier: the train **had** left.
items.explanation_cz: **By the time** se vždycky ohlíží na něco dřívějšího: the train **had** left.

items.en: He had just finished when I called.
accepts: He had just finished when I called.
items.explanation: **just** goes between had and the participle: had **just** finished.
items.explanation_cz: **just** patří mezi had a příčestí: had **just** finished.

items.en: The room was empty. Everyone had gone home.
items.cz: Místnost byla prázdná. Všichni šli domů.
items.gap: The room was empty. Everyone ____ home. (go)
accepts: The room was empty. Everyone had gone home.
items.wrong: The room was empty. Everyone went home.
items.explanation: The empty room is the later fact; the leaving came first, so **had** gone.
items.explanation_cz: Prázdná místnost je pozdější fakt; odchod byl dřív, proto **had** gone.

items.en: I didn't recognise her because she had cut her hair.
items.cz: Nepoznal jsem ji, protože si ostříhala vlasy.
items.gap: I didn't recognise her because she ____ her hair. (cut)
accepts: I didn't recognise her because she had cut her hair.
items.wrong: I didn't recognise her because she cut her hair.
items.explanation: The haircut came **before** the meeting: **had** cut. The participle of cut is **cut**.
items.explanation_cz: Účes byl **dřív** než setkání: **had** cut. Příčestí od cut je **cut**.

items.en: We had already eaten when they arrived.
accepts: We had already eaten when they arrived.
items.explanation: Dinner finished **before** they arrived. Participle of eat is **eaten**.
items.explanation_cz: Večeře skončila **dřív**, než přišli. Příčestí od eat je **eaten**.

items.en: I got up and made coffee.
accepts: I got up and made coffee.
items.wrong: I got up and had made coffee.
items.explanation: These two are told **in order**, one then the other. Past simple twice — no **had** needed.
items.explanation_cz: Tyhle dvě věci jsou **v pořadí**, jedna po druhé. Dvakrát minulý čas — **had** není potřeba.

items.en: She opened the door and walked in.
items.gap: She opened the door and ____ in. (walk)
accepts: She opened the door and walked in.
items.wrong: She opened the door and had walked in.
items.explanation: Door first, then in — already **in order**, so past simple. **had** would say it happened earlier, which is false.
items.explanation_cz: Nejdřív dveře, pak dovnitř — už je to **v pořadí**, takže minulý čas. **had** by říkalo, že to bylo dřív, což není pravda.

items.en: I had finished my work, so I went home.
items.cz: Dodělal jsem práci, tak jsem šel domů.
items.gap: I ____ my work, so I went home. (finish)
accepts: I had finished my work, so I went home.
I'd finished my work, so I went home.
items.explanation: The work finished **before** going home. Short form: **I'd** finished.
items.explanation_cz: Práce skončila **dřív** než cesta domů. Zkráceně: **I'd** finished.

items.en: By the time she called, I had gone to bed.
items.gap: By the time she called, I ____ to bed. (go)
accepts: By the time she called, I had gone to bed.
items.explanation: **By the time** she called, bed was already done: **had** gone.
items.explanation_cz: **By the time** zavolala, spaní už bylo hotové: **had** gone.

items.en: He said he had finished the report.
accepts: He said he had finished the report.
items.wrong: He said he has finished the report.
items.explanation: Reporting his words moves the verb one step back: *I have finished* becomes he **had** finished.
items.explanation_cz: Když opakuješ jeho slova, sloveso jde o krok zpět: *I have finished* se změní na he **had** finished.

items.en: They had never been to Prague before.
accepts: They had never been to Prague before.
items.explanation: **never** after had, and the participle of be is **been**.
items.explanation_cz: **never** za had a příčestí od be je **been**.

items.en: The shop was closed. It hadn't opened yet.
items.gap: The shop was closed. It ____ yet. (not / open)
accepts: The shop was closed. It hadn't opened yet.
The shop was closed. It had not opened yet.
items.explanation: Negative: **hadn't** + opened. The closed shop is the later fact.
items.explanation_cz: Zápor: **hadn't** + opened. Zavřený obchod je pozdější fakt.

items.en: When we got home, someone had broken the window.
items.cz: Když jsme přišli domů, někdo rozbil okno.
items.gap: When we got home, someone ____ the window. (break)
accepts: When we got home, someone had broken the window.
items.wrong: When we got home, someone broke the window.
items.explanation: The window went **before** we got home. Participle of break is **broken**.
items.explanation_cz: Okno se rozbilo **dřív**, než jsme přišli. Příčestí od break je **broken**.
